OFFICE OF OPERATIONAL STRATEGIC INITIATIVES
HOME/ Our Services/ Continuous Improvement/ LSS Scholarships
Scholarship Overview
We are proud to offer this opportunity for professional development.  Lean Six Sigma provides tangible
outcomes that impact our campus community.  We firmly believe in this as an investment in our staff
and community.
The LSS Green Belt course includes hands-on, instructor-led training at the UC San Diego Division of
Extended Studies. Training entails six full days of instruction over a three-month period. Green Belt
candidates will also complete a process improvement project that results in a minimum of $40K hard or
soft savings for campus and present their project work for evaluation approximately 6 weeks after the
last day of instruction.
For more information, please review the course details. 
Annual Application Information
The application window for FY 26/27 is anticipated to be in July or August.  More information will be
posted on this page as soon as it is available.  Please check back in June.  We also will make every
effort to spread awareness of this opportunity, including posting to Blink, emailing any past Yellow Belt
participants, and connecting to various newsletters.
This scholarship can only be applied to the project-focused LSS Green or Black Belt courses (the case-
study format is not eligible). Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will not
be considered during this review period.  A completed application includes both the submission and the
supervisor endorsement. 
Each applicant must submit their own application in IdeaWave, even if partnering on the same project
goal.  If partnering, please have the same title for your submission.
An Informational Session was be held on Tuesday August 19th 2025 and therecording can be viewed
here.
Please note that completing the Yellow Belt program is not a requirement, but it can provide a solid start
to your LSS journey, as well as assist in preparing for your project.
8/12/26, 8:30 AMLSS Scholarships
https://osi.ucsd.edu/services/continuous-improvement/scholarship.html1/5

Guidelines for Selecting Your LSS Project
The following attributes should be considered when identifying
possible Lean Six Sigma Green Belt projects:
1. Project results in an expected impact of at least $40K in hard or soft savings for UC San Diego
2. Your project should focus on an existing problem or opportunity that has the greatest potential to
improve customer satisfaction or enhance long-term performance
3. Your project addresses quality and waste issues such as defects, cycle time, over-processing,
excess motion/transportation, wait time, variability, etc.
4. The project falls within your job scope, is both quantifiable and measurable, and can be completed
within 12 weeks (3 months)
5. Sufficient data can be obtained within a reasonable amount of time
6. Project objectives have been reviewed and endorsed by your supervisor and other critical
stakeholders prior to applying for this scholarship
7. The improved process can be managed by the process owner using the control systems you
implement
The following scenarios should be avoided:
1. Sufficient data to evaluate process performance is not easily attainable
2. Implementation of already-established solutions such as software systems
3. Designing a new process, product or service from scratch
4. Projects that will not make a significant difference to your organization
5. Projects that do not have measurable goals
6. Projects that require more than 12 weeks (3 months) to complete
Selection Criteria
The LSS Green Belt program is best suited for staff members who are highly involved in business
process activities.  Applicants should have knowledge of basic statistics, project management, and team
leadership skills. Familiarity with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint is strongly recommended.
Applicants must have at least one year of service at UC and be career status. Supervisor support is
essential to the success of LSS candidates. The highest priority will be granted to applicants with:
Demonstrated experience and/or education with process improvement methodologies (as
indicated in your professional or personal statement). For example, previous formal training, being
part of the process improvement project team, implementing process improvements at work,
reading books, etc.
One to five years of experience in business analysis and/or project management
8/12/26, 8:30 AMLSS Scholarships
https://osi.ucsd.edu/services/continuous-improvement/scholarship.html2/5

One to five years in a current job position
Professional Level 2 equivalent or above. Exceptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis.
A viable process improvement project (see “Guidelines for Selecting Your LSS Project” section
above)
Demonstrated supervisor support
If you are awarded a scholarship, be advised that you may be asked to partner with a classmate on the
project. By accepting this scholarship, you authorize the UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies to
release your final project presentation to the Office of Operational Strategic Initiatives for reporting
purposes. Candidates will have the opportunity to request confidentiality for sensitive
information. Additionally, we will require that you attend a cohort launch discussion in advance of your
course. Once awardees are selected, OSI will coordinate with you to select an appropriate date and time.
This session is intended to build your support network and to provide any additional resources you may
need to be successful in your project.
Current Green Belt practitioners may apply scholarship credit towards the cost of the LSS Black Belt (or
accelerated Black Belt Course). You will be responsible for any costs beyond what the scholarship
covers for the Green Belt level course.
 
How to Apply for the Lean Six Sigma Scholarship
Once you have reviewed the information and selected a process, submit your application using this link.
See the embedded application process map below, created in Promapp, which outlines the steps for
preparing and applying for the LSS scholarship.  The map also includes video links and other resources.
8/12/26, 8:30 AMLSS Scholarships
https://osi.ucsd.edu/services/continuous-improvement/scholarship.html3/5

Additional resources
We are here to support you. Please reach us at OSI@ucsd.edu for questions regarding application
submission or UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies at processprograms@ucsd.edu for questions
regarding the program curriculum and schedule.
Please also review the resources below for more information:

Frequently Asked Questions

GB Scholarships 2025-2026

Application Process Questions:

Q: What are the steps in the scholarship process?

See the cool interactive process map here or read the boring text below.

Review our LSS Scholarships page for information and discuss the opportunity with your supervisor, and begin scoping a viable project.  Also, discuss the opportunity with your supervisor.

Once the application period begins, submit using the KualiBuild form.  Your supervisor will receive an email requesting additional information as part of the form’s workflow.

Upon receipt of your submission and supervisor support, your application is considered complete.  The committee will review submissions.

Scholarship evaluations will occur at the end of September and notifications of scholarship recipients will be sent out by early October. If awarded a scholarship, you will then work with UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies to select your class dates, attend classes, and work on your project. It is expected that you will provide updates on your project progress regularly and final results to OSI (more instructions will be provided if you are a scholarship recipient).

Q: Is this only for Green Belts? Or can I apply and use the scholarship for a Black Belt?

A: You may use the scholarship funds toward a Black Belt if you are a current Green Belt practitioner. You will be responsible for any costs beyond what the scholarship covers for the Green Belt level course. We encourage you to work with your supervisor to determine whether department funds can be used to meet this need.

Q: Are Health System employees eligible?

A: Yes! This opportunity is available to all UC San Diego career staff with more than one year of service.

Q: Can I use AI to help me with my submission?

A: Yes, but please use AI to help you, not to write generic fluff about process improvement.  You know the process best.  The goal is to use what you know about your process to help the committee understand why it would be impactful to review it as part of the certification. TritonGPT is an available resource for your submission, as well as a potential tool for improvement ideas, alongside many other UCSD approved AI tools.  You are also invited to watch this webinar, which discusses the overlaps and partnerships between AI and LSS.

Q: Can I apply for a scholarship if I have applied and/or received a scholarship in a previous year?

A: Yes. If you applied but did not receive a scholarship, you may apply again. If you applied and did receive a scholarship, your new application must be applied towards a Black Belt level project.

Q: Can I work with a partner on my project?

A: If you are applying for a Green Belt, you may work with a partner, but each scholarship applicant must submit their own individual application. As there are a limited number of awards available, individual submissions are preferred.  If you intend to apply for a Black Belt project, you must work individually.  

Q: How long will it take to find out if I was selected?

A: We anticipate all applicants will be notified by early October, but this will also depend on the number of applications we receive. 

Q: If awarded, does the scholarship need to be used right away?

A: The scholarship must be used within the 2025-2026 fiscal year.  This means the start date of your course should be within that window.

Q: If awarded, can the scholarship be used towards the online class?

A: Yes, however, the scholarship must be used towards the project-based sessions (not the case-study course).  We strongly recommend participating in the in-person format, based on past awardee feedback.

Project Selection Questions:

Q: How do I select a project?

A: Generally speaking, you should look at a process which you can impact and measure within a few months. You should be aware of a “problem” with the process (errors, customer complaints, delays, etc.). Don’t focus on how you are going to fix the problem because the intent is for you to learn Lean Six Sigma methodology and apply the tools to identify and continuously improve your process.

Q: How will I know if I can save $40k annually with my project?

A: Try not to worry too much about exactly how much savings you might achieve. Your improvements will not be discovered until you are in the class. Instead, consider data you do have regarding the current state. 

Consider the bullets below when thinking about savings potential:

How many times each month/year is the process used?

How long the process takes each time it is used?

What defects/errors arise along the way and how often do these occur?

What are the impacts if we do not find a better way to move through this process?

Are there any glaring areas of waste or rework?

Q: Do I need to have process maps, data, SOPs to submit with my application?

A: These and other resources are a helpful window to help the committee understand your process, but are not absolute requirements. The course will introduce process mapping and data gathering methods, but keep in mind that the overall project should be completed within three months, so having a solid understanding of the process beforehand will help you reach successful project outcomes.

Additional Resources:

Q: Do you have examples of previous projects?

A: Yes! Lean Six Sigma projects helped campus staff to: 

Saved 2,000 hours a year in the employee onboarding process. Learn more about the project in this video. 

Reduced event planning lead time by 81%. Learn about the project in this video.

A collection of awardees and project titles can be found at the bottom of our scholarships page.

Q: Do you have a completely fictitious example project I can look at so I can better understand how to fill out each section of the application?

A: Yes! But remember that this is a completely fictitious example, and you should only reference it for inspiration. Access it here.

Q: Do you have a visual to help me understand the application process?

 A: Yes! You may review the process map here. The map also is hyperlinked to the necessary internal resources such as KualiBuild, example submission, and our email address. 

Q: Is there someone I can contact with specific questions or to discuss project ideas?

A: Yes! OSI is here to support you. Reach us via email or we can meet in person or via Zoom to discuss project scoping, application requirements, or any other LSS questions. Please reach us at osi@ucsd.edu.

Thank you for submitting your application for the Lean Six Sigma Scholarship.  

The selection committee carefully reviewed your project proposal and supporting documents. It was very challenging for the committee to make its selections. We regret that we cannot extend a scholarship to you this year.

We commend you on your project proposal and commitment to driving towards a better campus.  We highly recommend that you stay involved in this important initiative.  Please see below for more opportunities: 

UC San Diego Extended Studies LSS Discount – Now that you have planned out an impactful project, we highly encourage you to keep going and fulfill that mission today.  Extended Studies will offer a $250 discount towards an upcoming LSS Green or Black program, to be used within 2025 - 2026.  For more information, please contact Angela Miller, Program Manager at ProcessPrograms@ucsd.edu.

UC San Diego Extended Studies Professional Development. You are eligible to receive a $100 discount towards the following courses: 

 Project Management Bootcamp or Project Management Essentials - https://extension.ucsd.edu/courses-and-programs/project-management-boot-camp 

Business Strategy - https://extendedstudies.ucsd.edu/courses/business-strategy-busa-41033 

Strategic Financial Management for Business Leaders & Entrepreneurs - https://extendedstudies.ucsd.edu/courses/strategic-financial-management-for-business-leaders-entrepreneurs-busa-41026 

For more information and to request a discount code, email ProcessPrograms@ucsd.edu.

Process Palooza – This fun event brings together change makers across the UC’s and beyond to learn, live and inspire. Attend, apply to compete, or donate your time to this fun celebration of lean culture at UC San Diego.  To learn more, please visit processspalooza.ucsd.edu.  

Yellow Belt and Promapp with OSI – If you have not completed the Yellow Belt LSS course, we encourage you to participate in an upcoming session. OSI also supports a process mapping tool known as Promapp.  Please visit the OSI Pages for more information. https://osi.ucsd.edu/

The selection committee greatly appreciates your time and commitment to continuous improvement at UC San Diego and hopes that you will continue this important work.

Please feel free to contact me should you have any questions.  

Regards,

Antonio “Tony” Nava

Programs Director

Operational Strategic Initiatives

I am delighted to inform you that you have been selected to receive a scholarship for the Lean Six Sigma course at UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies! Sponsorship of this opportunity has been made possible by the Office of Operational Strategic Initiatives and the Office of the Vice Chancellor, CFO.

Lean Six Sigma (LSS) provides a systematic method to improve performance efficiencies and to reduce variations in business operations to achieve productivity and profitability gains. This certificate includes both classroom training and hands-on practicum. Course details can be found at: UCSD DES - Green Belt

The 2025/2026 LSS Green Belt class schedule is as follows:

LSS Green Belt

Fall 2025 – Section 1: In-Person. Thursdays, 9:00am – 3:00pm on 10/2, 10/16, 10/23, 10/30, 11/6; Project Presentations Jan 15, 2026. Taught by Tracy O’Rourke.

Fall 2025 – Section 2: Live Online. Fridays, 9:00am – 12:00pm on 10/10, 10/17, 10/23, 10/31, 11/14, 11/21, (No Class 11/7); Project Presentations Jan 8, 2026. Taught by Sabine Rentschar.

Winter 2026—Section 3: Live Online. Fridays, 9:00am – 12:00pm on 1/31, 2/7, 2/14, 2/21 & 2/28, 3/7; Final Presentations – 5/16/2025. Taught by Tracy O'Rourke.

Next steps:

If you do not already have an Extended Studies Student ID number, click here to create. 

Indicate your preferred course session, as well as a backup option, by emailing processprograms@ucsd.edu. Please email your Student ID number and your preference no later than October 1st.

Process Programs will register you based on the available seating, and they will email you confirmation of your registration. 

You are also invited/encouraged to participate in Yellow Belt as an introduction (or as a refresher) and Promapp.  

As you move through the class and your project, OSI will be an available resource in addition to the support of your instructor.

Submit your project outcomes and total savings to OSI before the date of your final presentation.

Be advised that there is limited availability in each session and enrollment is on a first come-first served basis. Please select a backup option in case your first choice is not available and ensure that you discuss the timing with your supervisor so that your project is ready to go when the course begins. The project will allow you to apply the learned tools and show quantifiable results. Your instructor will mentor you from the start until completion of a successful project. If you have any questions regarding this or any other aspects of the course, please contact Angela Miller, Program Manager at ProcessPrograms@ucsd.edu or click here to Schedule an Appointment. 

By accepting this scholarship, you agree to authorize UC San Diego Extended Studies to release your final project presentation to the Office of Operational Strategic Initiatives for reporting purposes. If you indicate that your project contains sensitive data, we will check in with you before sharing any details/information publicly.

Congratulations, 

Antonio “Tony” Nava

Programs Director

Fictitious Example Project for GB Scholarships

Project Name

Provide a catchy name for your project, to get us in the right mindset.

“Boulevard of Broken Workflows”

Process Overview

Help the review committee gain an understanding of the current state. What are the general steps in the process? Who are the stakeholders and what is their experience? What data is available or needed regarding the process cadence, process times, defects? Are there any complexities to navigate?

The current BIR (Broken Item Replacement) process in my department, OSI, is inefficient, leading to prolonged wait times and customer dissatisfaction. Internal customers are experiencing delays, with some requests taking over three months to resolve. These delays also open us up to audit risks, especially when the item that needs replacement is related to policy mandates. To address this issue, I aim to analyze the current process, identify patterns and areas for improvement, and implement changes to reduce cycle times. I will utilize existing reporting tools, including a live Excel document and ticketing system data, to understand the bottlenecks and inefficiencies in the replacement process. 

The replacement process affects multiple departments, with a wide array of items needing replacement. To focus our efforts, we may consider prioritizing departments with the highest request volume or those with significant verbal feedback.  We have partners in procurement that can help us understand the upstream considerations, but we aim to keep any proposed changes to steps within our control.

Interest Statement

What is your exposure/experience with Lean or Six Sigma? What drives you and what do you hope to gain from the Green or Black Belt?

After introducing myself to LSS through Yellow Belt training and personal research, I'm eager to apply these skills to improve customer satisfaction and turnaround time in my department. With experience as a team lead and a natural inclination towards problem-solving and process improvement, I believe this class will help me drive meaningful change and prepare for a leadership or project management role.  Attending Process Palooza this year was a blast, and I am eager to learn more.

Scoring the person and not necessarily the project.  The project scoring helps us determine whether the candidate understands how to scope a problem statement, display impact, etc.

Consider greater weight to the candidate and supervisor than the project.  Perhaps a minimum threshold on the project.  If they score high on the personal and did not jump to improve, and it is in their area – maybe that should matter more than the project potential impacts?
